name: Cleveland-Cliffs iron ore and Toledo HBI
description: Captive Minnesota/Michigan pellet mines and the Toledo hot-briquetted iron plant. HBI is assumed (not verified) to supply part of the Butler EAF charge for GOES.
size_label: Toledo nameplate 1.6M t/yr HBI; GOES-attributable flow est. $12-32M

name: Ferrous scrap processors and transformer dismantlers
description: Scrap processors (incl. Cliffs-owned FPT), pig iron importers and transformer recyclers (A-Line, TCI of Ohio, Sunbelt's ~1,000 units/day). Supply low-residual metallics to EAF mills.
size_label: Transformer-derived recovered metal est. $100-350M/yr (all metals); the GOES-melt scrap edge is general scrap, not transformer-derived

name: Ferroglobe
description: Largest US ferrosilicon and silicon-metal producer (Beverly OH, Calvert City KY). GOES carries ~3% Si added as ferrosilicon; supply to Cliffs is inferred.

name: Imported ferrosilicon, MgO and coating chemicals
description: Imported FeSi (Elkem, Brazil, Malaysia; limited by the 2025 AD case), high-purity MgO annealing separator (e.g., Tateho) and phosphate/colloidal-silica insulation coatings for GOES.

name: Freeport-McMoRan Arizona copper mines
description: Morenci, Bagdad, Safford and others feed the Miami AZ smelter; anode is refined at El Paso.

name: Rio Tinto Kennecott
description: Integrated Bingham Canyon mine, smelter and refinery near Salt Lake City; one of few US sources of mined and refined cathode.

name: Imported refined copper (Chile, Peru, Canada)
description: Codelco, Glencore, Teck and others cover a large share of US cathode use. Section 232 refined-copper duty of 15% (2027) and 30% (2028).

name: Bauxite and alumina suppliers
description: Alumina for US and Canadian smelters (~2 t per t of aluminum): Alcoa refineries, Century's Jamalco and third-party supply.

name: Softwood pulpwood and soybeans
description: Long-fibre softwood for unbleached kraft pulp (transformerboard, insulating paper) and US soybeans crushed for natural-ester FR3 fluid.

name: Naphthenic crude oil suppliers
description: Imported and Gulf Coast low-wax naphthenic crudes run by Ergon (Vicksburg MS), Calumet (Shreveport/Princeton LA) and others.

name: Imperial Recycling (Imperial Group, incl. Midwest Industrial Metals, Exeon Processors)
description: Fulton's family metals group (founded 1962). Recovers copper and aluminum from insulated, armored and oilfield cable; Midwest Industrial Metals (Northlake IL) buys non-ferrous scrap; Exeon (Jonesboro IN) granulates wire into clean chops; growing PVC jacket recycling.

name: Cleveland-Cliffs (Butler Works GOES, carbon sheet)
description: The only US and North American GOES producer (Butler PA melt/roll, Zanesville OH finish); a $170M project ($75M DOE grant) adds ~25% GOES by 2028. Also sells carbon sheet for distribution tanks and cabinets.
size_label: GOES revenue est. $0.5-0.95B (120-160k MT); 2025 stainless+electrical shipments 552k net tons

name: Nippon Steel
description: Leading high-permeability GOES maker; Japan is the main GOES source for Canadian and Mexican core makers and a top origin of direct US coil imports. Owns U.S. Steel (no GOES).

name: POSCO
description: Korean GOES producer; Korea was the #2 origin of direct US coil imports (Commerce). Assumed main GOES source for Korean-owned US plants.

name: Other GOES and amorphous (JFE, Baowu, thyssenkrupp, Metglas)
description: JFE Steel (Japan), China Baowu (tariff- and EO 14421-limited), thyssenkrupp Electrical Steel, and Metglas (Proterial; Conway SC, ~45 kt/yr amorphous ribbon, mostly exported).

name: Freeport-McMoRan El Paso refinery and rod mills
description: Refines Miami smelter anode into cathode and casts continuous rod at El Paso TX and Miami AZ for wire makers.

name: Southwire (copper rod)
description: Largest US copper rod producer (SCR mill, Carrollton GA); specifies LME Grade A cathode for magnet-wire rod.

name: Grupo Mexico copper (Asarco, Southern Copper)
description: Asarco's Amarillo TX refinery and rod plant plus Southern Copper's Mexican cathode; the assumed domestic source for Mexican magnet-wire makers.

name: Primary aluminum (Rio Tinto Aluminium, Alcoa, Century)
description: Quebec hydro smelters (largest source of US primary imports), Alcoa US/Quebec smelters and Century (Mt. Holly SC, Sebree KY) supplying rollers of winding strip and foil.

name: Electrical-grade kraft pulp and insulating paper mills
description: Unbleached softwood kraft pulp for transformerboard plus insulating kraft, crepe and thermally upgraded papers; much is imported from Nordic mills.

name: Nucor (plate mills)
description: EAF plate mills at Hertford NC, Tuscaloosa AL and Longview TX near the Southeastern transformer cluster; scrap-fed, closing a loop with transformer recycling.

name: Other plate and sheet mills (SSAB, Steel Dynamics, AM/NS Calvert, Algoma, Ternium)
description: Hot-rolled, cold-rolled, galvanized sheet and plate for tanks, covers, radiators and enclosures. Names are typical mills, not confirmed suppliers.

name: Ergon (HyVolt naphthenic transformer oil)
description: Largest NA naphthenic refiner (Vicksburg MS, Newell WV). Raised naphthenic prices +$2.05/gal in Mar-Apr 2026; $400M Vicksburg expansion (+20% crude) due Q1 2027.

name: Cargill (Envirotemp FR3 natural ester)
description: Leading soybean-based natural-ester dielectric fluid, originated at Cooper Power (now Eaton); 100+ US utilities use ester-filled units. 2026 expansions were in Europe and Turkiye only.

name: Other transformer oils (Nynas, Shell Diala, Calumet)
description: Nynas Nytro (imported from Europe), Shell Diala inhibited and GTL oils, and Calumet naphthenic grades; weighted to power transformers and global OEMs.

name: Imperial Aluminum-Minerva and Imperial Alloys (Imperial Group)
description: Secondary aluminum smelter in Minerva OH converting scrap into die-cast and foundry alloys. Does not make EC-grade (1350) winding aluminum.

name: Worthington Steel: Tempel and Corefficient
description: Largest NA merchant core maker. Tempel's Burlington ON plant (~US$85M, opened Jun 2026) doubles transformer-core output; Corefficient (Monterrey) is a Kloeckner Metals unit, likely under Worthington since it took ~62% of Klöckner on Jun 3, 2026.

name: Other merchant core makers (Mexico, Canada, US)
description: Smaller Mexican and Canadian core shops (Canada 52%, Mexico 45% of 2019 US core imports) plus US slitters and core makers such as MK Magnetics and Magnetic Metals. US core imports reached ~$524M in 2025 (secondary); that figure also includes Tempel Canada and Corefficient output, shown under Worthington.

name: Essex Solutions (magnet wire and CTC)
description: Largest NA magnet-wire maker (ex-Essex Furukawa); reshaped Simcoe ON to add CTC lines for transformer customers.

name: Sam Dong America / Sam Dong Ohio
description: Korean-owned conductor maker: $13.5M CTC and enamel expansion at Rogersville TN (Sep 2026) and $13M at Delaware OH lifting oxygen-free rod casting from 5.5M to 14M lb/month.

name: Magnekon (Viakable / Xignux)
description: Large Monterrey magnet-wire plant serving transformer and motor makers in Mexico, the US and Canada; sister company of Prolec's former 50% owner Xignux.

name: Other conductors: imported CTC, Rea/Elektrisola, aluminum strip and foil
description: Imported CTC and paper-covered conductor (Asta, Korean, Indian, Chinese makers), Rea Magnet Wire (Elektrisola) and aluminum winding strip, foil and wire for distribution units.

name: Weidmann Electrical Technology
description: Main NA transformerboard (pressboard) mill and component plant, St. Johnsbury VT; a $40-50M expansion adding >30% capacity opened May 27, 2026.

name: Other insulation: Arclin Nomex, Krempel, kit converters, imports
description: Arclin (bought DuPont Aramids, Nomex, ~$1.8B, Apr 1 2026) for dry-type insulation, plus kraft/crepe/DPE paper, laminated wood and pressboard parts from Krempel, converters and imports.

name: Maschinenfabrik Reinhausen
description: Dominant on-load tap changer (OLTC) maker; Humboldt TN plant expanded 45% with further OLTC expansion under way; plans to double global capacity by 2030.

name: Hitachi Energy components (Alamo bushings, tap changers, Canduct)
description: Alamo TN (>$100M expansion) is becoming NA's largest bushing plant (to 800 kV); plus tap changers and Canduct insulation kits (London ON, Boardman OH; acquired Jul 2, 2026). Mostly captive.

name: Trench Group (HSP bushings)
description: Carved out of Siemens Energy in 2024. Its >$60M Charlotte NC plant (25-765 kV bushings, 3,500/yr expandable to 10,000) opened Jul 2026 and is ramping: the main new merchant bushing capacity. Hubbell's PCORE (LeRoy NY) is another US merchant bushing maker; Hitachi's Alamo TN plant is mostly captive.

name: Qualitrol (Ralliant)
description: Transformer gauges, pressure relief, temperature monitors and online DGA; >4M grid devices installed. Most monitoring revenue comes from utility retrofits.

name: Radiators and coolers (Trantech, Menk, imports)
description: Trantech Radiator Products (leading NA panel-radiator maker) plus imported radiators and forced-oil coolers (Menk, Mexican, Korean, Indian makers).

name: Independent tank and enclosure fabricators (US, Mexico)
description: Contract fabricators of tanks, conservators, pad-mount cabinets and structures (e.g., Washington Metal Fabricators, Acero ATD). Most large builders make tanks in-house; importers and new plants outsource.
size_label: Outsourced est. $170-800M of a $1.4-3.0B tank pool

name: Coatings (PPG, Sherwin-Williams)
description: Liquid and powder primer/topcoat systems for tanks, radiators and pad-mount cabinets. Shot-blasting abrasives (Ervin, Metaltec, Winoa) precede painting.

name: Foundries and machine shops (castings, valves, terminals)
description: Aluminum and steel castings, bushing flanges, drain and sampling valves, terminal pads, wheels and lifting hardware; fragmented regional suppliers.

name: Barnhart Crane & Rigging
description: Heavy-haul and rigging contractor with its own fleet; e.g., moved a 485,500 lb transformer 500+ miles from the Port of Los Angeles to Nevada.

name: Other heavy haul, rail and ports (Lone Star, Mammoet, Bigge, Emmert, Sarens, Schnabel rail)
description: Modular-trailer and jack-and-slide moves, Schnabel-car rail (~30 NA cars, weak source) and port handling of imported LPTs. NA heavy-move spend est. $0.3-1.3B.

name: Field installation contractors (SDMyers, Shermco, OEM crews)
description: Site assembly, vacuum oil filling and commissioning of new units subcontracted by builders, especially importers without US crews.

name: Metaltec Steel Abrasive Company
description: Cast steel shot and grit made from melted scrap (Canton Township MI); one of three leading US abrasive makers. Tanks, radiators and enclosures are shot-blasted before painting.
ownership: Imperial Group, Lorentzen, Ashland Capital (Fulton, Aug 2022)

name: Stainless Foundry & Engineering (SFE)
description: Milwaukee stainless and high-alloy sand and investment castings (to ~200 lb) for energy, nuclear and power-generation OEMs; ~6-week lead times.

name: AFCO Industries
description: Aluminum, composite and vinyl building products plus CNC fabrication and contract manufacturing in Alexandria LA, Olive Branch MS, Pell City AL and Olmstead IL. Not a pressure-tight tank shop.
ownership: Fulton Asset Management and Ashland Capital (closed Jul 31, 2025)

name: Panther Metalflow
description: Swiss-type CNC turning and Metalflow zinc cast-in-place assemblies (Walled Lake MI); ISO 9001, ITAR. Could make terminals, studs and bushing hardware.

name: Transend Logistics
description: Chicago 3PL and freight broker: flatbed, dry van, drayage, cross-dock and cross-border Mexico-US-Canada lanes. No heavy-haul or Schnabel capability.

name: Hitachi Energy
description: Largest LPT supplier into NA: South Boston VA, Crystal Springs MS, Varennes QC plus imports; >$1B US build-out (South Boston $457M 2028-29, Gallman MS $528M 2029). Most vertically integrated (own bushings, tap changers, Canduct).

name: Siemens Energy (Transformers)
description: Supplies LPTs and GSUs mainly from Mexico, Brazil and Europe; first US LPT plant, Charlotte NC ($150M, 24-57 units/yr), slipped to 2027.

name: HD Hyundai Electric
description: Korean EHV leader with a Montgomery AL plant; plant #2 ($200M, +50% EHV, 765 kV test) due 2027. Q2 2026 operating margin 25.1%.
size_label: NA revenue ~$1.3-1.7B incl. reactors, switchgear and distribution units (Q2 2026 KRW 541.9B annualized = ~$1.55B); transformer edges est. $0.5-0.9B

name: Hyosung HICO
description: Memphis TN plant (ex-Mitsubishi), one of very few US plants building 765 kV units, plus Changwon imports; $208-238M expansions (+50% by 2028). Booked $287M of 765/345 kV orders from two US tech companies (Sep 2026), with deliveries likely in 2027-29.
size_label: US revenue ~$0.9-1.1B (2025) incl. reactors and breakers

name: Virginia Transformer Corp (VTC)
description: Largest US-owned power-transformer maker: 6 NA plants (US, Mexico), ~2-500 MVA. Rincon GA +50% by Mar 2027; holds WAPA's single-award LPT blanket purchase agreement; explored a >$6B sale in 2025.

name: Pennsylvania Transformer and Niagara (Quanta)
description: Quanta's transformer units: PTT (5-750 MVA to 765 kV, Canonsburg PA and Raeford NC; pad-mount plant from 2027) and Niagara Power Transformer (Cheektowaga NY; $71.2M expansion). Supports the AEP-Quanta EHV development agreement.

name: Delta Star
description: Engineered power transformers and mobile/unitized substations (Lynchburg VA, San Carlos CA, Saint-Jean QC; >1,400 staff). MacLean Power Systems agreed to buy it Sep 1, 2026 (close Q4).
ownership: Private, pending sale to MacLean (Blackstone, Centerbridge)

name: LS Electric
description: Korean exporter; 2026 US data-center orders of $132M (345 kV) and ~$115M (switchgear and distribution transformers) from unnamed big tech/hyperscalers.

name: Other imported power transformers (Iljin, Mexican, Brazilian, European, Indian, Turkish)
description: Power units from makers not shown separately. Mexico, Brazil and Korea supplied 57% of >100 MVA import units in 2025; Korea >10 MVA exports to the US were $738M.

name: Prolec GE (GE Vernova)
description: Largest NA transformer maker (distribution to large power): Monterrey, Goldsboro NC (220 to 420 units/yr by 2027), Shreveport LA, Waukesha WI. GE Vernova took 100% on Feb 2, 2026 ($9,656M total consideration).

name: WEG Transformers North America
description: Three Washington MO plants (560 staff) plus Mexico and Brazil; $77M expansion adds 50% of 1-10 MVA capacity.

name: SGB-SMIT / Southwest Electric
description: Bought Southwest Electric (Oklahoma City; substation and specialty units) in Mar 2025; imports power units from Europe. On AEP's EHV vendor list.

name: Eaton (Cooper Power)
description: Distribution, 3-phase pad-mount, substation and dry-type units from Waukesha WI and Nacogdoches TX; Jonesville SC ($340M, 700 jobs) in 2027. Electrical Americas data-center sales +65% organic.

name: Howard Industries
description: Largest US distribution maker (~4,000 staff, 14 MS sites) with in-house core lines; moving up to 250 MVA/345 kV at Ellisville by end-2026.

name: ERMCO
description: Co-op-owned distribution maker (TN, AR; Spire dry-type); 566k sq ft Waddell AZ 3-phase plant opens 2027. Sells to co-ops directly and via RESCO.

name: Central Moloney
description: Single-phase pole and pad-mount maker (Pine Bluff AR, Panama City Beach FL); sells mostly via distributors such as Border States; JEA FY26-29 awardee.

name: Forgent Power Solutions (VanTran, MGM)
description: Listed maker of transformers (VanTran Waco TX, MGM Vernon CA), switchgear and switchboards. FY26 revenue $1.42B (+89%), 59% data center; $3.0B backlog; FY27 guide $2.4-2.6B.

name: JST Power Equipment (Jinpan)
description: US arm of China's Hainan Jinpan: pad-mounts in Wytheville VA (1,000/yr from 2027), switchgear in Lake Mary FL, plus dry-type and imports. EO 14421 exposure.

name: Imported distribution transformers (Taiwan, Canada, Mexico, Korea; Eaglerise)
description: Imports supply 25-30% of US distribution units (CRS): Korean makers Kerec, Sungjin, Taihan (Austin Energy contracts), plus Eaglerise's new US/Mexico plants (won Lafayette LA bids 18-23% below distributors).

name: Hammond Power Solutions
description: Leading NA dry-type maker (Canada, US, Mexico). Q2 2026 sales +44.7%, adj. EBITDA 16.4%; backlog +96.9% YoY on data centers but -6.9% QoQ.

name: Other dry-type makers (Schneider/Square D, Siemens, ABB, ELSCO, Jefferson)
description: LV/MV dry-type and cast-resin units sold with switchgear packages through electrical distributors to commercial, industrial and data-center buyers.

name: Sunbelt Solomon
description: Largest US transformer remanufacturer: new and rebuilt units, rentals, temporary power and field service from 42 locations (>1,600 staff); recycles ~1,000 units/day. TJC agreed to buy it Jul 20, 2026 (close pending).
ownership: Trilantic North America, pending sale to TJC

name: Field repair and regional reman (IPS/Belyea, Midwest Electric Transformers, others)
description: IPS (bought Belyea's HV refurbishment and portable-substation business Oct 7, 2026) and small rewinders that rebuild distribution and small power units in 4-12 weeks vs 40-50 for new pad-mounts.

name: Giga Energy
description: Former bitcoin-mining infrastructure firm supplying MV transformers, switchgear and modular data-center power; Houston plant (1,000+ units/yr) started 2026.

name: Solid-state transformer startups (Heron Power, Amperesand, DG Matrix)
description: Heron ($140M Series B; Morgan Hill CA factory late 2027; RWE Americas pilot), Amperesand ($80M; 30 MW to hyperscale AI customers in 2026) and DG Matrix ($60M, ABB-backed).

name: American Electric Power (AEP)
description: Largest US transmission system and most 765 kV. $72B 2026-30 capex; Nov 2025 development agreement with Quanta to expand domestic EHV transformer capacity; approved 500-765 kV vendors include Hitachi, HICO, SMIT and Siemens.

name: Duke Energy
description: Largest US IOU by customers. $17.2B annual sourcing, ~$1B with NC suppliers in 2025 including GE Vernova transformers from Goldsboro.

name: Other IOUs and transmission companies (Southern, Oncor, Dominion, Xcel, FPL, PG&E, others)
description: Remaining IOUs and transcos. EEI puts 2026 IOU capex at $239B; transformer buying est. 3.5-6% of capex. Oncor has secured Permian LPTs (first deliveries Q1 2027); Dominion adds substation units for NoVA data centers; Xcel cites transformer delays.
size_label: Other-IOU transformer purchases est. $7.2-12.3B/yr (all-IOU $8.4-14.3B less AEP and Duke)

name: Public power and federal utilities (munis, JEA, Austin Energy, TVA, WAPA, BPA)
description: ~2,000 municipal utilities and state authorities plus TVA and federal PMAs. Buy substation units directly and distribution units through bids (JEA FY26-29, Austin Energy $200M NTE) and distributors.
size_label: ~15% of US retail kWh; transformer purchases est. $0.7-1.8B/yr (assumed 3.5-6% of capex)

name: Electric cooperatives
description: ~830 distribution and ~60 G&T co-ops owning ~42% of US distribution lines; buy through co-op-owned ERMCO and distributors such as RESCO and Border States.

name: Wesco International (incl. Anixter)
description: Largest US electrical distributor; resells transformers to utilities (incl. Sourcewell) and dry-type units to contractors. Public-power transformer sales fell in 2025 on inventory normalization.

name: Sonepar North America (Stuart C. Irby)
description: Irby resells GE/Prolec and other transformers to munis and IOUs (JEA, Austin Energy, Zeeland awards); Sonepar's electrical branches sell dry-type units to contractors.

name: Other distributors (Border States, RESCO, Gresco, Graybar, CED)
description: Regional utility-supply and electrical distributors that resell distribution and dry-type units to munis, co-ops, contractors and industrial buyers; frequent bidders on municipal tenders.

name: Data-center developers, colos, neoclouds and their EPCs
description: QTS, Vantage, Crusoe, CoreWeave, Equinix, Digital Realty, Stack, Aligned and others, plus EPCs procuring for hyperscaler self-builds. Buy main-substation, MV/LV pad-mount and dry-type units (~$0.08-0.20M of transformers per MW).

name: NextEra Energy Resources
description: Largest US renewables and storage developer (~33 GW backlog; record 4 GW contracted Q1 2026). Says it has purchased transformers through 2030; up to 10 GW of gas from ~2028.

name: Other generation developers and EPCs (Invenergy, AES, Intersect, RWE, gas IPPs)
description: IPPs and their EPCs (Blattner, Mortenson, Kiewit, Primoris) buying GSUs, collector-substation and MV step-up units for solar, wind, BESS and gas; ~50-160 US GSUs/yr from the gas-turbine backlog.

name: Industrial, LNG and oil and gas buyers
description: LNG terminals, refineries, chemicals, mining, semiconductor and battery fabs, and Permian electrification buying unit-substation, substation and GSU units directly or via EPCs.

name: Microsoft
description: Leases and rents much of its capacity (CoreWeave, Nebius) besides self-built campuses; sells Azure compute to OpenAI and Anthropic.
size_label: CY2026 capex ~$190B; self-build transformer content est. $80-400M/yr

name: Alphabet (Google)
description: Mostly self-builds; sells TPU capacity to Anthropic. Agreed to buy Intersect Power (background knowledge).

name: Amazon (AWS)
description: Mostly self-builds; Anthropic's primary cloud and training partner and a $38B OpenAI supplier.

name: Meta Platforms
description: Self-builds gigawatt campuses, rents from CoreWeave and buys solar and storage PPAs from NextEra and Invenergy.

name: Oracle (OCI)
description: Builds OpenAI's Stargate capacity mainly through leased campuses (e.g., Crusoe's Abilene TX).

name: Hyperscalers and AI campuses unnamed in transformer orders
description: Direct transformer orders disclosed only as from 'US big tech' (Hyosung $287M, HD Hyundai ~$721M framework, LS Electric ~$247M). Buyers are among the named hyperscalers, xAI and AI labs; shown separately to avoid guessing.

name: US residential electricity customers
description: ~145M household accounts; 1.51T kWh in 2025.

name: US commercial electricity customers (incl. many data centers)
description: Offices, retail, hospitals, schools and data centers billed as commercial; 1.49T kWh in 2025. Data centers used ~312.6 TWh in 2025.

name: US industrial electricity customers
description: Manufacturing, mining and process industry; 1.04T kWh in 2025.

name: OpenAI
description: Rents compute from Microsoft, Oracle, AWS and CoreWeave rather than owning most data centers.

name: Anthropic
description: Rents compute from AWS (primary), Google TPUs and Microsoft Azure.

name: Enterprises renting cloud and colocation (North America)
description: Companies and public bodies buying IaaS/PaaS and colocation, excluding AI-lab mega-contracts. LBNL projects data centers at up to 11.8% of US electricity by 2030.

name: Household final demand (incl. EVs, heat pumps)
description: Household consumption of electricity-dependent goods and services, including electrification of transport and heating.

name: Demand for US-made goods (reshoring)
description: Buyers of domestically made goods, including new fabs, battery plants and process industry that pull industrial load.
